title: Operation Paul Bunyan
summary: Josh and Chuck discuss Operation Paul Bunyan, the August 1976 Korean DMZ "axe murder" incident. They cover the Korean division and the DMZ and Joint Security Area (JSA), the Bridge of No Return, and the lightly guarded tense patrol culture there. The hosts then describe the poplar tree that blocked the line of sight between UN Command checkpoints, the August 18, 1976 tree-pruning party led by Captain Arthur Bonifas, and the North Korean attack led by Lieutenant Pak (Pochoul) that killed Bonifas and First Lieutenant Mark Barrett. They describe the US response: Kissinger's push for force, the Washington Special Action Group, General Richard Stilwell's plan, the show of force with B-52s, nuclear-armed aircraft and carriers, the August 21 tree-cutting operation with chainsaws, the resulting stump, and China and USSR signals of non-intervention. They also cover the Kim Il Sung planting claim, circumstantial evidence the attack was planned, the 1986 memorial, the 2002 peace pine tree, the 1984 defection firefight, and the most dangerous golf hole. The episode ends with a listener email about Saturday morning cartoon preemptions.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts joke about their clothing and introduce the topic of Operation Paul Bunyan.

segments.title: Korean division and the DMZ
segments.summary: Post-World War II division of Korea at the 38th parallel, the Korean War and armistice, and the DMZ with the village of Panmunjom and the Joint Security Area.

segments.title: Joint Security Area and Bridge of No Return
segments.summary: Describes the JSA as the place where the two Koreas meet, the Bridge of No Return, and the provocations patrols faced, along with the UN Command rules of engagement.

segments.title: Captain Bonifas and the JSA provocations
segments.summary: Profile of Captain Arthur Bonifas, the intimidation tactics used in the JSA, and the 1976 incident in which Major Henderson was attacked after the North Koreans provoked him.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts take a break and banter about puns.

segments.title: The poplar tree and the tree-pruning party
segments.summary: The poplar tree blocked the line of sight between UN checkpoints. After South Korean workers were chased off, a team led by Captain Bonifas went to prune it on August 18, 1976. Lieutenant Pak Chol arrived with North Korean guards, and the tree's supposed link to Kim Il Sung was discussed.

segments.title: The axe attack and deaths of Bonifas and Barrett
segments.summary: Pak ordered the attack. Captain Bonifas was killed with an axe and First Lieutenant Mark Barrett was beaten to death. Bonifas was due to go home in three days. These were the first US and UN Command deaths in Korea since the war.

segments.title: US response and Kissinger's push for force
segments.summary: Henry Kissinger, Secretary of State under Gerald Ford, favored a violent response. The Washington Special Action Group considered options. Kissinger was reportedly the only one pushing for force, and Ford was during the Republican convention and an election year against Jimmy Carter.

segments.title: Operation Paul Bunyan show of force
segments.summary: General Richard Stilwell commanded the operation. Forces were raised to DEFCON 3 and included helicopters, B-52s, nuclear-armed F-111s, and naval ships. The hosts discuss the scale of the show of force and the Cold War risk of World War Three.

segments.title: Chinese and Soviet signals and the South Korean commandos
segments.summary: China and the USSR signaled they would not intervene. South Korean commandos with claymore mines blocked the bridge in a provocative stance that was not coordinated with UN Command.

segments.title: Tree cutting on August 21 and the stump
segments.summary: On August 21, 1976, the tree was cut to a ten-foot stump by engineers with chainsaws in about forty-five minutes. The stump looked like surrender, and Kissinger reportedly wanted it carved into a middle finger. Kim Il Sung expressed regret for the deaths.

segments.title: Aftermath, DMZ border changes, and 1984 defection firefight
segments.summary: The JSA was reorganized and the military demarcation line enforced. A 1984 defection firefight that killed three North Korean soldiers and one South Korean soldier is mentioned. Kissinger was disappointed by the limited result.

segments.title: Memorial, peace pine tree, and planned-attack evidence
segments.summary: The poplar stump was removed in 1986 and replaced with a memorial plaque. The 2002 Pine Tree of Peace, the most dangerous golf hole, and circumstantial evidence that the attack was planned (Radio Pyongyang's quick report and a nonaligned nation meeting) are discussed.

segments.title: Listener mail: pain of preemption
segments.summary: A listener named Michael Crandall writes about Saturday morning cartoons being preempted by sports on local channels. The hosts read the email and joke about the name.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: Hosts give the email address and sign off with the show's credits.
